title_en: On the Inscription of the Titles
author: Eustathius of Antioch
occasion: The surviving fragments explain the meaning of the stone pillar that Jacob set up at Bethel, interpreting it as a prophecy of Christ, the cross, and the two peoples. The work appears to be a theological exposition of the biblical narrative for a Christian audience.
argument: Eustathius argues that Jacob's pillar at Bethel was not an idolatrous stele but a divinely inspired prophecy. The stone and the ladder vision prefigure Christ's body, the cross, and the church as the house of God and gate of heaven. The oil poured on the stone points to the anointing of Christ's feet and to his burial, while the stone itself signifies Christ as the rejected cornerstone. Finally, the two nations announced to Rebecca are interpreted as Jews and Christians, with the older people serving the younger.

outline.move: Eustathius distinguishes Jacob's pillar from idolatrous steles, explaining that Jacob saw in the vision the bodily form of Christ and the victorious trophy of the cross.
He explains that the ladder resembles the cross, and that the stone Jacob set up as a pillar was an image of the face that appeared to him, called the house of God and the gate of heaven.
He interprets the oil poured on the stone as signifying the anointing of Christ's feet and Christ's burial, and the stone itself as the rejected cornerstone.
He interprets the two nations and two peoples announced to Rebecca as Jews and Christians, with the older people serving the younger, and concludes that Jacob is shown enthroned with the Holy Spirit.

cast.name: Jacob
cast.who: The patriarch whose vision and pillar at Bethel are the subject of the treatise.

cast.name: Christ
cast.who: The Son of God, whose body, cross, and burial are prefigured in Jacob's vision and pillar.

cast.name: Mary
cast.who: A woman named Mary who anointed Christ's feet with ointment; the source does not identify her further.

cast.name: Moses
cast.who: The biblical author cited for the story of Rebecca and the two nations.

cast.name: Rebecca
cast.who: The mother of Jacob and Esau, to whom the Lord announced the two nations in her womb.

key_terms.sense: A stone pillar or monument set up as a memorial, here specifically Jacob's pillar at Bethel.
The ladder in Jacob's vision, interpreted as a figure of the cross.
The cross of Christ, prefigured by the ladder and called the victorious trophy.
The temple or house of God, applied to Christ's body and the church.
The gate of heaven, a title given to the stone and by extension to Christ.
The cornerstone rejected by the builders, identified with Christ.
The oil poured on the pillar, signifying the ointment poured on Christ's feet and Christ's burial.
The two nations announced to Rebecca, interpreted as Jews and Christians.
The two peoples from Rebecca's womb, identified as the Jewish and Christian peoples.
Idolatry, the false worship associated with the steles of Jacob's opponents.
A trophy or victory monument, applied to the cross.
The house of God, a title given to the stone and interpreted as Christ's body.

scripture: The author cites the Septuagint (LXX) and uses its book names and Psalm numbering. Citations should be given in modern form, e.g., Genesis for the story of Jacob and Rebecca, and Psalms for the cornerstone quotation.
uncertain: The exact date of composition is unknown.
The original addressee or audience is not stated in the surviving fragments.
The full original structure of the work is lost; only fragments survive.
The identity of the Mary who anointed Christ's feet is not specified in the source.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The Son of God (quoted), introduced by 'ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐξέφηνεν ὁ τοῦ Παντοκράτορος Υἱός' and quoted directly
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οἶκον δὲ Θεοῦ προσειπὼν αὐτὸν, ᾐνίττετο τὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Λόγου ναὸν ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐξέφηνεν ὁ τοῦ Παντοκράτορος Υἱός· λύσατε τὸν ναὸν τοῦτον καὶ ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις ἐγερῶ αὐτόν.
_unresolved_facts.fix: The Son of God (quoted), introduced by 'ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ἐξέφηνεν ὁ τοῦ Παντοκράτορος Υἱός' and quoted directly; but the quotation is actually the words of Christ (the Son) about the temple, not Eustathius quoting the Son about something else. The brief should clarify this is Christ's own words about his body as temple.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Scripture (quoted), introduced by 'ἔφη' and quoted directly; the words are from Proverbs
_unresolved_facts.fix: Scripture (quoted), introduced by 'ἔφη' and quoted directly; the words are from Proverbs 11:29 LXX (δουλεύσει ἄφρων φρονίμῳ), though the exact form here is slightly variant.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Mary, a woman named Mary who anointed Christ's feet with ointment; the source does not identify her further
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: τοῦτο μὲν ἐκείνου δηλωτικὸν ἦν οὗ διεπράττετο σπουδαίως ἡ Μαρία, μύρον ἐξ ἄκρων ἐπιχέουσα τοῖς τοῦ Χριστοῦ ποσίν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Mary, a woman named Mary who anointed Christ's feet with ointment; the source does not identify her further. Note: The source says she poured oil 'ἐξ ἄκρων' (from the top/extremities), not that she is the same figure as the Mary of Bethany in the Gospels, though this is the likely allusion.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He interprets the two nations and two peoples announced to Rebecca as Jews and Christians, with the older people serving the younger, and concludes that Jacob is shown enthroned with the Holy Spirit
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἐντεῦθεν τοίνυν ἐπὶ θρόνου προύγραφεν αὐτὸν τοῦ ἁγίου καθέζεσθαι, δηλῶν ὅτι σύνθρονος ἀποδέδεικται τῷ θειοτάτῳ Πνεύματι διὰ τὸν οἰκοῦντα Θεὸν ἐν αὐτῷ διηνεκῶς.
_unresolved_facts.fix: He interprets the two nations and two peoples announced to Rebecca as Jews and Christians, with the older people serving the younger, and concludes that Jacob is shown enthroned with the Holy Spirit—meaning he is made co-enthroned with the Holy Spirit because God dwells in him continually.
